verification.note: test_pdf_vertical_acceptance.py:339-366 puts NESTEDVERTICALWORD (18 non-space chars, rotate=270) and NESTEDHORIZONTALWORD (20 chars) on one source page, and the source page is embedded as a form on both pages. Page 1 adds 'H', giving 21 horizontal characters. Page 2 adds two long horizontal lines. Vertical characters never outnumber horizontal ones, so 'counts[0] > counts[1]' at pdf.py:117 is false on both pages. Only the mixed-page append branch (pdf.py:124-134) runs. The whole-page replacement branch (pdf.py:117-123) is never run on text nested in an LTFigure. The recursion in text_boxes (pdf.py:85-90) is shared by both branches, so the code appears correct, but the test does not cover the predominantly vertical case that I10 also requires. I read the code and test only. Nothing was run.

specification_compliance: I10 is implemented: text_boxes (pdf.py:85-90) recurses into LTFigure at any depth, and both the predominant-vertical and mixed-page branches use it.
The (0,1) and (1,0) direction counts use the 0.01 tolerance and ignore other directions (pdf.py:112-115), as the r4 revision requires.
regression_risks: The predominant-vertical branch with nested figure text has no test, so a regression there would not be caught.
test_coverage: The nested-form test covers only the mixed-page path. It would need a page where vertical characters outnumber horizontal ones inside a form XObject.
